name: Netdata
description: Netdata agent reads over its v1 REST API: node info and version, the chart catalogue, currently-raised alarms, and the recent data points of one named chart. Read-only; Netdata's agent API exposes no write surface, and this connector wires none. The agent API is unauthenticated by default (base_url is the only credential); put it behind a reverse proxy for exposure beyond a trusted LAN.

tools.name: node_info
tools.description: Get the Netdata node's identity and capacity: version, OS, CPU/RAM, uptime, how many charts and metrics it collects, and which hosts it mirrors

tools.name: list_charts
tools.description: List the charts this Netdata agent collects, each with its id, title, units, chart type and update frequency

tools.name: list_alarms
tools.description: List the alarms currently raised on this node (warning or critical), with their chart, value, status and recipient

all.description: When true, list every configured alarm and its state, not only the currently-raised ones

tools.name: chart_data
tools.description: Get the recent data points of one chart by id (e.g. system.cpu, system.ram, disk.io), as timestamped rows across the chart's dimensions

chart.description: Chart id, e.g. system.cpu, system.ram, system.load (from list_charts)

after.description: Relative start in seconds, negative for a window back from now (e.g. -300 for the last 5 minutes); default -60

points.description: How many time buckets to return (default 20)

needs_review: AUTH IS none BY DESIGN: the Netdata agent's local API on :19999 ships with no authentication, so base_url is the only credential and auth.type is 'none'. This is Netdata's documented default (https://learn.netdata.cloud/docs/netdata-agent/securing-netdata-agents); an internet-exposed agent must sit behind a reverse proxy, which is a deployment concern, not a spec one. base_url fromCredential keeps a real credential referenced so the spec is not credential-less.
READ-ONLY: all four tools are GET, write:false. The Netdata agent v1 API is read-only by nature (metrics, charts, alarms); there is no mutating endpoint to model.

list_charts and node_info return large objects (a busy node has hundreds of charts); the picks keep the summary fields plus the charts/alarms maps, capped by response.truncate. charts is kept as the whole map rather than flattened because Connector Spec v1 has no computed fields to reshape a keyed object into an array.

list_alarms with all=true returns every configured alarm and its state; on a fresh container the raised set is empty but the configured set is not, so all=true gives a non-trivial 200. Without all, a healthy node returns a 200 with an empty alarms object, which is still a valid proof.

chart_data probes system.cpu, which every Netdata agent collects from boot, over a fixed -60s/5-point window. The honest expected live result is a 200 with a small labels+data matrix. after is relative seconds (Netdata's own convention), so no absolute timestamp is baked.

LIVE-PROOF CONTRACT: node_info / list_charts take no input (_probe {}); list_alarms pins all=true; chart_data pins system.cpu. No credential is hinted (there is none). Proven against docker netdata/netdata (v2.11.0 nightly), then destroyed.

API VERSION: this uses the stable v1 API, which Netdata keeps for backward compatibility alongside newer v2/v3 endpoints. v1/info, v1/charts, v1/alarms and v1/data are the long-standing, widely-deployed surface; the newer /api/v2 and /api/v3 shapes are deliberately not used so the connector serves older agents too.
rateLimit 60/min: Netdata is a per-second collector and cheap to poll, so the local courtesy cap is higher than the 30/min default; Netdata enforces no request rate limit of its own.
